svg.title: RIEMANN · MAP R5 — Theta lifts, periods and the Siegel-Weil formula: every statement of the chapter, and what each one rests on
svg.desc: The blueprint's chapter 5 in one poster: its 61 statements as cards, each with the Lean declaration it stands for, the statement in words, how its proof goes, and what it uses and is used by. Read it from the foot up: the chapter's theorem, thm-theta-inputs, is at the bottom, and every card stands above the cards whose proofs use it. An arrow from A to B says that the proof of B uses A; a dashed arrow says that the proof of B names A without listing it as a use. The statements that head a section or a group of results have full cards; the others are drawn shorter. Map mode: nothing of the blueprint's text or the proof's source is quoted. No Lean was built: see diagram R1, band 5.

A → B: the proof of B uses A (the arrow takes A's colour)
A ⇢ B: the proof of B names A without listing it as a use (dashed)

Title and pill. The title is the blueprint's; the pill gives the kind and the provenance: new in Alpöge's proof, modified from a published result, or published as it stands. Main.lean marks the theorems the

The line in italics gives the statement's id and how many paragraphs the blueprint spends on its statement and its proof. The text itself is not quoted: it is the blueprint's authors', and the blueprint link in the
footer has it. The Lean signature is not quoted either, for the same reason; the footer gives the declaration's name, file and line in the mirror.
Stated with, Proof uses and Used by are the blueprint's edges, in full. An arrow from A to B: the proof of B uses A, and the arrow takes A's colour.

text.tspan: 2 · The chapter, from its leaves down to its theorem

svg.text: 16 rows. Section by section the chapter runs: 1. The Siegel-Weil formula (8); 2. Theta towers and their step identities (4); 3. Non-vanishing and separation of theta lifts (7); 4. Rational test vectors (7); 5. L-values along Witt towers and the indefinite slope bound (4); 6. The isometric period identity (7); 7. Bessel transforms and archimedean models (7); 8. The off-diagonal bound (8); 9. Counting automorphic forms and mass constants (4); 10. Valuations of periods and CM theta measures (4). The cards keep that
order within a row where the arrows allow.
